request.deadline: 12-month delivery period from August 2026 to July 2027
deliverables: Periodic independent audits of treasury fund use and oversight metrics
Eternl Core rewrite, Eternl Hub, enhanced hardware wallet support, enhanced wallet data export, and governance tooling improvements
request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund 12 months of Eternl operations, maintenance, support, infrastructure, audits/oversight metrics, and continued development while Eternl introduces paid Pro plans.

claims.claim: Eternl is a non-custodial Cardano light wallet for web, browser extension, Android, and iOS used for payments, staking, governance, and DApp interaction.
The proposal asks for ₳2,350,000, valued at about $0.1787 per Ada, to cover around $420,000 of annual operating cost.
The requested budget is allocated as ₳1,292,500 frontend, ₳587,500 backend, ₳117,500 support, ₳305,500 admin, and ₳47,000 audits.
Eternl has an install base of about 100,000 browser-extension installs and about 30,000 Android and iOS installs combined.
If roughly 5,500 users, or about 4.2% of the install base, buy a Pro plan, Pro-plan income would fully cover the annual $420,000 cost.
The proposer says up to $420,000 worth of Ada will be converted into stablecoins and deposited into a public company wallet, with any Ada above that amount returned to the treasury.

The proposer commits to semiannual repayment checks where surplus remaining treasury stablecoins plus paid-plan income above $420,000 are used to repay the treasury until $420,000 in Ada has been repaid.
The audits allocation is for independent audits of treasury fund use in February 2027 and August 2027, not for technical security audits.
Eternl claims that 10-18% of Cardano mainnet transactions are conducted via Eternl.
The main Eternl UI will not be open-source, though some libraries used by Eternl will be published through the npm registry.

summary: The document presents a ₳2.35 million treasury request for one year of Eternl operations and development, with a sustainability plan based on paid Pro subscriptions, public-wallet custody, repayment conditions, and non-technical financial audits, but many adoption, impact, feasibility, and risk claims are asserted without independent evidence in the anchor text.
